I think the right direction forward for voat is three-fold.
* Users can only be banned within a subverse for actions within that subverse. * Subverses belong to the users. The mods are just custodians and are there to serve the users. This is more of a philosophical point, but it gives the admins standing to step in when the mods get out of control.
* A method to filter content.that requires less initial setup and less maintenance than the current "block subverse" method. Maybe apply some default filtering for non-logged in users.

One possible solution is shareable block-lists for subverses. When you create an account, you're given the option to subscribe to a selection of popular user-created block-lists.

A better solution than shareable block-lists would be an AI based vote scoring system. Things the software thinks you will vote up will get pushed to the top. Things the software thinks you will vote down will get pushed down. The software would try to predict what you want to see and show that to you based on your voting history. (If Alice and Bob vote similarly, and Alice and Carol vote completely differently, Bob's votes count for more than Carol's votes when viewed by Alice.) Unfortunately, this would be computationally very expensive.
